outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the covering number of convex bodies has moved only as bounds: a single-author preprint of 20 Sep 2026 (unreviewed, v1 only) proves the 2^d bound for the fractional illumination number and gives covering number H(d) <= 2^d(d log d + d log log d + O(d)) for large d; separate preprints give small-dimension upper bounds (2024), and cap-body covering claims for one class (Oct 2025, revised Aug 2026); the 2^n covering conjecture itself remains open for every n >= 3 in all sources read.
problem_asks: (1) For every n and every bounded convex body K in n-dimensional Euclidean space, K can be covered by at most 2^n smaller positive homothetic copies of itself (copies lambda*K with 0 < lambda < 1); this is the universal upper bound claimed for all n. (2) Equality case: the bound 2^n is needed only when K is an affine image of the n-cube (a parallelepiped). Notes on the frozen wording: the Wikipedia lead and disambiguation text read '2n', which is a rendering loss of 2^n; the sources read treat the bound as 2^n. The homothetic wording of the bullet (copies lambda*K) is not the only form in use: much of the literature (Huang et al.; Arman, Bondarenko and Prymak) defines the covering number H_n with translates of the interior of K. The two forms are treated as the same quantity in the literature, but I did not verify that equivalence from a source. Parts (1) and (2) are the whole of what the bullet asks; the n = 2 case is settled, n >= 3 is open.

events.what_happened: F. W. Levi (Archiv der Mathematik, 1955) proved the planar case: every bounded planar convex set is covered by four smaller positive homothetic copies, and four are needed only for parallelograms. Wikipedia lists Levi's paper as the earliest source for the problem; Hadwiger (1957) and Gohberg and Markus (1960) state the general question.
events.delivers: Settles the n = 2 case completely: covering number H_2 = 4, equal to the conjectured 2^2, with equality only for parallelograms.
events.remains: Every n >= 3 (open in all sources read).

checked_by.who: F. W. Levi (author); the n = 2 case is recorded as settled in the monographs cited on Wikipedia (Boltyanski and Gohberg 1985; Brass, Moser and Pach 2005)
checked_by.qualification: Original author; those monographs are the standard references for the area
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the planar proof; the monographs record the case as settled. I did not open Levi's paper or the monographs.

events.directly_checkable: The planar covering statement can be checked by hand. I did not check it.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for n = 2 (consistent with 2^n).

events.what_happened: Papadoperakis (Geometriae Dedicata, 1999, per the Wikipedia reference list) showed that every 3-dimensional convex body is covered by 16 smaller homothetic copies (H_3 <= 16). Prymak and Shepelska (arXiv 1811.08962, 2018) describe this as the best known 3D bound and build on Papadoperakis's approach. The original paper was not opened.
events.delivers: Upper bound H_3 <= 16 in dimension 3 only.
events.remains: H_3 = 8 (the conjectured value) and every n >= 4 for general bodies.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (paper not opened; publication is taken from the Wikipedia reference list)

events.direction: Upper bound only; cuts toward 2^3 = 8 being achievable only by later work.

events.what_happened: Lassak (Proc. AMS, 1988, 'Covering the boundary of a convex set by tiles', per the Wikipedia reference list) gives the upper bound (n+1)n^(n-1) - (n-1)(n-2)^(n-1) for the covering number in small dimensions; Wikipedia says this beats the asymptotic bounds for small n. The original paper was not opened. The 3D centrally symmetric case is attributed to Lassak in a search summary; I did not verify that from the original.
events.delivers: Explicit upper bound on the covering number for small n given by the formula above (for n = 3 it gives 34, far above 8; for n = 2 it gives 6, above 4).
events.remains: The conjecture 2^n for all n >= 3; the formula is far from 2^n in small dimensions.

checked_by.qualification: Original author; refereed journal of record
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the bound (paper not opened; taken from the Wikipedia status section)

events.direction: Upper bound only, weaker than 2^n for every n >= 2 that I evaluated.

events.what_happened: Artstein-Avidan and Slomka (arXiv 1310.7892, submitted 29 Oct 2013, revised 15 Dec 2013; Israel Journal of Mathematics 2015 per a search summary, not opened) define weighted covering numbers. They bound the Levi-Hadwiger covering problem for centrally symmetric convex bodies, qualitatively the same as the best previously known bound, and settle the centrally symmetric case of Naszodi's equivalent fractional illumination conjecture, including the equality case.
events.revisions: v2 15 Dec 2013; journal version per search summary (not opened).
events.delivers: Restricted to centrally symmetric bodies: the weighted analogue, a fractional-illumination bound for symmetric bodies, and the Levi-Hadwiger covering bound for symmetric bodies. Symmetric-class result; no bound on the covering number for general bodies.
events.remains: All non-symmetric bodies, and the unweighted covering conjecture for general bodies in every dimension.
events.time_since_posted: about 13 years (29 Oct 2013 to the session date)
events.direction: Analogue (weighted/fractional) and symmetric-class; consistent with 2^n for symmetric bodies, but does not address the covering statement for general bodies.

events.what_happened: Prymak and Shepelska (arXiv 1811.08962, submitted 21 Nov 2018; revised 8 Jan 2020 and 29 Sep 2020; J. Geom. 111:42, 2020) use Papadoperakis's approach to show H_4 <= 96, H_5 <= 1091 and H_6 <= 15373, where H_n is defined in the abstract by smaller homothetic copies (and equivalently by illumination).
events.revisions: v2 8 Jan 2020; v3 29 Sep 2020; journal J. Geom. 111:42 (2020).
events.delivers: Upper bounds on H_4, H_5, H_6 (the covering number in dimensions 4 to 6). No exact value.
events.remains: Exact values for n >= 4, and the conjecture H_n = 2^n for all n >= 3.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (journal version not opened; the arXiv abstract was read)

events.direction: Upper bounds only; far above 2^n in dimensions 4 to 6 (for example 1091 against 32 at n = 5).

events.what_happened: Huang, Slomka, Tkocz and Vritsiou (arXiv 1811.12548, submitted 30 Nov 2018; J. Eur. Math. Soc. 24 (2022) 1431-1448) prove that the translative covering number N(n) (covering by translates of the interior) satisfies N(n) <= C(2n, n) e^(-c sqrt(n)) for a universal c > 0, improving the bound C(2n, n) n ln n that had stood for over sixty years. They also obtain an exponential improvement for psi_2 bodies and for bodies with positive modulus of convexity.
events.revisions: v2 6 Dec 2020 (references updated, remark on Ehrhard's conjecture added); journal version JEMS 24 (2022).
events.delivers: General-n upper bound for the translative covering number, a sub-exponential improvement on C(2n, n) n ln n. This is still far above 2^n, since C(2n, n) is of order 4^n. Exponential improvement for psi_2 bodies and bodies with positive modulus of convexity.
events.remains: The conjecture N(n) = 2^n for every n >= 3, and the general-body bound of order 2^n.

The abstract I read does not state the value obtained, and I did not read the full text.

events.what_happened: Prymak (arXiv 2112.10698, submitted 20 Dec 2021; v2 20 Sep 2022; published as 'A New Bound for Hadwiger's Covering Problem in E^3', SIAM journal, 2023 per Wikipedia and a search listing) shows that every 3-dimensional convex body is covered by 14 smaller homothetic copies (H_3 <= 14). The method modifies Papadoperakis's approach: a discretisation reduces the problem to feasibility of a finite family of linear programs with rational data, checked in exact arithmetic with SageMath scripts (about 4,660,035 LP instances, about two weeks on 10 threads, per the arXiv HTML).
events.revisions: v2 20 Sep 2022; SIAM journal version (2023 per Wikipedia; DOI 10.1137/22M1490314 per a search listing; the SIAM page was not opened).
events.delivers: Dimension-3 upper bound H_3 <= 14 (improving 16). Not equality with the conjectured 8.
events.remains: H_3 = 8 (the conjectured value) in dimension 3, and every n >= 4.

events.what_happened: Campos, van Hintum, Morris and Tiba (arXiv 2206.11227, submitted 22 Jun 2022; IMRN 2024 per the Wikipedia reference list) prove that for any convex body K in R^d, exp(-Omega(d/(log d)^8)) * 4^d translates of int(K) suffice to cover K, an almost-exponential improvement on the earlier O(4^d sqrt(d) log d). They also show that a positive answer to Bourgain's slicing problem would give an exponential improvement for the conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (per the arXiv abstract page); IMRN 2024 journal version.
events.delivers: Asymptotic translative covering bound for every convex body: N(d) <= exp(-Omega(d/(log d)^8)) * 4^d. Built on the Chen-Klartag-Lehec results for Bourgain's slicing problem, as the abstract states.
events.remains: The conjectured 2^d bound. The result is 4^d times an exponentially small factor, which does not reach 2^d for any d in the range the implicit constant covers.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (IMRN 2024, per the Wikipedia reference list; journal page not opened)

events.direction: Asymptotic upper bound for general bodies; moves the general-d bound from 4^d sqrt(d) log d to 4^d exp(-Omega(d/(log d)^8)); still far from 2^d.

events.what_happened: Joos (arXiv 2305.00569, submitted 30 Apr 2023, v2 23 May 2023, 'Covering the Crosspolytope with Crosspolytopes') computes the covering functional gamma_m^d(K^d) for the d-dimensional crosspolytope K^d and several values of m (for example gamma = 1 for m < 2d with d >= 4). Its abstract states: 'Moreover the Hadwiger's covering conjecture is verified for the d-dimensional crosspolytope.'
events.delivers: As the abstract states, the covering conjecture is verified for the d-dimensional crosspolytope, with exact covering-functional values stated for d >= 4. Class-restricted to the crosspolytope.
events.remains: Every other convex body in every dimension, including the general statement.

events.what_happened: Arman, Bondarenko and Prymak (arXiv 2304.10418, submitted 20 Apr 2023; v2 3 Apr 2024; v3 26 Jun 2024) show that there are convex bodies of constant width in E^n with illumination number at least (cos(pi/14)+o(1))^(-n), answering a question of G. Kalai about illumination of constant-width bodies. The abstract does not mention Hadwiger's covering conjecture. It also proves that some finite sets of diameter 1 cannot be covered by (2/sqrt(3)+o(1))^n balls of diameter 1.
events.revisions: v2 3 Apr 2024 and v3 26 Jun 2024 (both after the frozen revision; v3 marked 'minor revision').
events.delivers: Exponential lower bound on the illumination number of constant-width bodies. This concerns a class (constant-width bodies) and the illumination number, not the covering number H_n for all bodies. It is a different question from the bullet's covering statement.
events.remains: Covering conjecture for all bodies in every n >= 3 (this paper does not address it).
events.direction: Different question (constant-width class, illumination number). The exponential base (cos(pi/14))^(-1), about 1.026, is far below 2, so it is not a counterexample to the 2^n bound for this class, but it does not bear on the covering conjecture for general bodies.

The formula was not visible in the abstract page read. No arXiv version was found, so the journal publication date is used.

events.what_happened: Arman, Bondarenko and Prymak ('On Hadwiger's covering problem in small dimensions', arXiv 2404.00547, submitted 31 Mar 2024) define H_n as the minimal number of interior translates of an n-dimensional convex body needed to cover it, and H_n^s for symmetric bodies. They note that the Hadwiger covering conjecture predicts H_n = H_n^s = 2^n, and prove upper bounds from covers by translates of John's ellipsoid: H_5 <= 933, H_6 <= 6137, H_7 <= 41377, H_8 <= 284096, H_4^s <= 72, H_5^s <= 305, H_6^s <= 1292. Published in Canadian Mathematical Bulletin 68(4) (2025, online 4 Apr 2025). A Cambridge erratum (17 Apr 2026) corrects only the corresponding author's name and email.
events.revisions: arXiv: v1 only. Journal: Canadian Mathematical Bulletin 68(4) (2025), DOI 10.4153/S0008439525000384, online 4 Apr 2025. Erratum online 17 Apr 2026 (DOI 10.4153/S0008439526101957): corrects the corresponding author's name and the contact email only; no mathematical change.
events.delivers: Upper bounds on the translative covering number H_n for n = 5, 6, 7, 8 and on the symmetric numbers H_4^s, H_5^s, H_6^s. These move the named quantity for those dimensions, but they are upper bounds, far above the conjectured 2^n (for example 933 against 32 at n = 5).
events.remains: Exact values of H_n for n >= 3 in every dimension, including n = 5 to 8; and the conjecture for general n.

events.what_happened: Arman, Kaire and Prymak ('Illumination number of 3-dimensional cap bodies', arXiv 2507.08712, submitted 11 Jul 2025; v2 29 Jan 2026 marked 'Referee's comments incorporated'; Discrete Mathematics 349 (2026), no. 7, 115025) prove that every 3-dimensional cap body has illumination number 6 (below the conjectured 8). The proof uses probabilistic arguments and integer linear programming (a SageMath script, under 2 hours on a personal computer). The paper's own Theorem 2 reads 'For any cap body K in R^3, I(K) <= 6'. The Introduction calls the covering conjecture the Hadwiger-Boltyanski illumination conjecture and says Boltyanski showed it equivalent to an illumination problem; the paper itself states no covering number.
events.revisions: v2 29 Jan 2026 ('Referee's comments incorporated'); journal Discrete Mathematics 349 (2026) 115025.
events.delivers: Illumination number of the class of 3D cap bodies is 6 (<= 8). This is the illumination formulation, for a class of bodies. The paper does not state a covering number for them.
events.remains: Covering number of 3D cap bodies as a covering statement; all convex bodies in dimension 3 and every n >= 4.

events.what_happened: Arman, Kaire and Prymak ('Hadwiger's conjecture for cap bodies', arXiv 2510.25968; v1 29 Oct 2025; v2 13 Dec 2025 (terminology change, 'spike' in place of 'cap' per a search summary); v3 18 Aug 2026, the version read) claim to confirm Hadwiger's covering conjecture for cap bodies in all dimensions. The paper's stated theorems are upper bounds on the illumination number I of cap bodies: I(K) < 2^n for 4 <= n <= 15 (computer-assisted exact LP, with values I(K^4_c) <= 11, I(K^5_c) <= 17, I(K^6_c) <= 27, I(K^7_c) <= 44, I(K^8_c) <= 66), I(K) < n + 7 + (sqrt 2)^n sqrt(pi n)(...) for n >= 9 (which gives < 2^n for n >= 13), and Corollary 3: I(K) < 2^n for n >= 3, which the paper says 'imply that the Hadwiger conjecture is valid for all cap bodies'. Its Introduction identifies H(n) with the illumination number of the class of all convex bodies; the step from an illumination bound to a covering is not written out.
events.delivers: Asserts the covering conjecture for the class of cap bodies in every dimension (the paper's claim), via illumination bounds I < 2^n for n >= 3. Class-restricted (cap bodies, a class defined in the paper, whose definition I did not read). Exact covering number for cap bodies is not stated.
events.remains: Covering conjecture for general convex bodies in every dimension; exact covering number of cap bodies; the illumination-to-covering step is asserted, not written.

events.what_happened: Yegor Gorodzha ('Fractional illumination and the optimal exponential rate in Hadwiger's covering conjecture', arXiv 2609.23913, submitted 20 Sep 2026, v1 only, single author; math.MG, math.CO) proves two results. Theorem 1: every convex body K in R^d satisfies I*(K) <= 2^d, with equality iff K is an invertible affine image of the cube [-1,1]^d (a parallelotope); I* is Naszodi's fractional illumination number. Theorem 2: as d tends to infinity, the covering number H(d) of R^d by smaller positive homothetic copies satisfies H(d) <= 2^d (d log d + d log log d + O(d)) with an absolute implicit constant, so H(d) = 2^(d + O(log d)). The abstract describes this as 'establishing the optimal exponential rate in Hadwiger's covering conjecture'. The main argument is credited to OpenAI's GPT-6 Pro (see ai). The title footnote thanks Gil Kur and Steven Hoehner 'for their help in presenting this work'; this is not described as checking the proof.
events.delivers: Theorem 1 (fractional quantity I*, a changed quantity from the covering number): the 2^d bound for all convex bodies in every dimension, with equality exactly for parallelotopes. Theorem 2 (covering number H(d)): an asymptotic bound for large d, 2^d times a polynomial factor, i.e. base 2 up to d^(O(1)) factors. This moves H(d) from the earlier 4^d exp(-Omega(d/(log d)^8)) (Campos et al. 2022) to 2^(d+O(log d)) for large d. It does not establish H(d) <= 2^d for any d, and it does not give the covering number exactly for any d.
events.remains: The covering statement H(d) <= 2^d for every d >= 3, and its equality case for the covering number (parallelotopes). The fractional result does not by itself give a covering bound; the covering bound is only asymptotic with a polynomial-in-d factor.
events.time_since_posted: about 3 weeks (20 Sep 2026 to the session date 11 Oct 2026); no later citing or commenting work found in searches
events.directly_checkable: Theorem 1 is an inequality on fractional illumination covers of convex bodies; the author's covering measure (minimising an overlap energy) and greedy covering on a finite net are described in the abstract. I did not check the proofs.
events.direction: Fractional analogue: proves the 2^d bound in full for I*(K) (Naszodi's conjecture; cuts toward the conjecture). Covering number: upper bound 2^d times polynomial factor for large d, which cuts toward the conjecture asymptotically but does not prove it.

systems.what_it_did: Per the author's title footnote, the main argument was found in conversation with the model. Appendix A says the ideas behind the paper were discovered in that chat; the model was never directed to prove the fractional illumination conjecture; the fractional result 'seemingly emerged as an intermediate step towards a different goal set out for the LLM in the prompts'; and 'a later request to attack the full conjecture led to the greedy covering argument on a finite net used for the asymptotic bound'. The author states they take full responsibility for the mathematical claims. Codex was used afterwards to revise the exposition and check sources (not recorded as a system here, see summary).

summary: Searches (36 queries) and page reads (32 pages opened, listed below; several PDFs did not decode) found no event that settles the 2^n covering conjecture for any n >= 3. The bound history is recorded as events: Levi (1955) settles n = 2; Papadoperakis (1999) gives H_3 <= 16; Lassak (1988) a small-n formula; Artstein-Avidan and Slomka (2013) the symmetric and weighted case; Prymak and Shepelska (2018) H_4 to H_6; Huang et al. (2018) a sub-exponential general bound; Lian and Zhang (2021) the 3D crosspolytope, value not read; Prymak (2021) H_3 <= 14, computer-assisted with exact LPs; Campos et al. (2022) 4^d exp(-Omega(d/(log d)^8)); Joos (2023) the crosspolytope class; Arman, Bondarenko and Prymak (2023) the constant-width illumination lower bound (a different question); Chen, Gao and Wu (January 2024) the cross-polytope with 2^n translates. In the window: Arman, Bondarenko and Prymak (arXiv 31 Mar 2024; CMB 2025) give H_5 <= 933, H_6 <= 6137, H_7 <= 41377, H_8 <= 284096 against conjectured 32, 64, 128, 256 (upper bounds, human-authored, SageMath-computed, no AI); the April 2026 erratum changes author metadata only. Arman, Kaire and Prymak (arXiv 29 Oct 2025, v3 18 Aug 2026) assert the covering conjecture for cap bodies in all dimensions; their theorems bound the illumination number (I < 2^n for n >= 3; computer-assisted exact LP for 4 <= n <= 15), the covering step is asserted from an equivalence in the Introduction and not written out, and the only independent engagement found is a co-author's talk. The most consequential in-window item is Gorodzha (arXiv 20 Sep 2026, single author, v1 only): Theorem 1 gives I*(K) <= 2^d with equality for parallelotopes (Naszodi's fractional conjecture, a changed quantity), and Theorem 2 gives H(d) <= 2^d(d log d + d log log d + O(d)) for large d, i.e. the covering number up to 2^(d+O(log d)), which improves the 4^d-base bound but does not reach 2^d. AI: the title footnote says 'The main argument was found in conversation with OpenAI's GPT-6 Pro'; Appendix A says the fractional result 'seemingly emerged' as an intermediate step and that the greedy covering argument came from a later request in the same conversation; Codex revised exposition and checked sources (not load-bearing, so not in ai.systems). I read this through the HTML rendering returned by the fetch tool (the PDF body did not decode); the linked shared chat returned only its title ('ChatGPT - Derive New Hadwiger Bound'), so the transcript was not read. The footnote and Appendix A do not say which argument is 'the main argument' or whether the overlap-energy covering measure came from the model. Close calls: (a) the bullet's smaller-homothets form versus the translative form (translates of int K) used by Huang et al., Campos et al. and Arman et al.; Wikipedia states the homothetic form; I did not verify the equivalence from a source, and a bound in one form may not transfer to the other; (b) whether a bound on the fractional or illumination quantity moves the named covering quantity (Gorodzha Theorem 1; cap-body illumination bounds); (c) whether the cap-body illumination bounds establish the covering statement the paper asserts. Discounted as different questions, with their AI attributions recorded: graph-theoretic Hadwiger items (Costa et al.; Kuhn et al.; Girao et al.; Norin and Steiner, whose graph proof is credited to GPT-6 Astra); the spherical Hadwiger classification (Wang and Wu, credited to OpenAI Codex); OpenAI's covering-density item and its graph counterexample, known only from secondary sources because the PDFs did not read. No AI system is credited with the covering number itself other than the Gorodzha disclosure. No priority dispute found; the fractional conjecture is attributed to Naszodi in Gorodzha and in the Artstein-Avidan and Slomka abstract.
competing_reading: For reading Gorodzha as moving the named problem: H(d) is the named quantity, Theorem 2 changes its exponential base from 4 (Campos et al.) to 2 for large d, the author calls the rate optimal, and the 2^d fractional result is the conjecture's natural weighted form, which the author proves in full. Against it: the bullet asks for H(d) <= 2^d for every n, and no such bound is proved; the 2^d proof is for the fractional quantity, an analogue; the covering bound is asymptotic with an implicit constant and a polynomial factor; and the author-credited AI origin is recorded as disclosed, with the appendix saying the fractional result 'seemingly emerged', not that a method was designed. For reading the cap-body paper as settling the covering conjecture for cap bodies: the paper claims it, and its Corollary 3 uses an I < 2^n bound that the Introduction equates with covering. Against it: the paper's theorems are illumination bounds, and the step from illumination to covering is asserted rather than written out. For the translative form versus the homothetic form: the literature uses both, and treating them as one quantity is the standard reading, but I did not verify that equivalence.
what_would_settle_it: For Gorodzha: an expert reading of the proofs of Theorems 1 and 2 (the overlap-energy covering measure and the greedy net argument), and whether the covering bound's polynomial factor can be removed; the shared transcript at https://chatgpt.com/share/6aa156f6-e0f4-83eb-9532-bd258660e44b, to see which steps the model supplied and whether the 'main argument' is the fractional result or the covering argument; the PDF Appendix A text, to check the quoted wording. For cap bodies: the illumination-to-covering step written out, and an independent rerun of the SageMath/LP certificates for 4 <= n <= 15. For the translative and homothetic forms: a source proving the covering numbers coincide for every convex body (or a body where they differ). For the OpenAI catalogue items: the PDFs themselves, to see whether the covering-density and graph-counterexample papers make any claim about the 2^n covering number.

event.what_happened: Arman, Kaire and Prymak ('Illumination number of 3-dimensional cap bodies', arXiv 2507.08712, submitted 11 Jul 2025; v2 29 Jan 2026 marked 'Referee's comments incorporated'; Discrete Mathematics 349 (2026), no. 7, 115025) prove that every 3-dimensional cap body has illumination number 6 (below the conjectured 8). The proof uses probabilistic arguments and integer linear programming (a SageMath script, under 2 hours on a personal computer). The paper's own Theorem 2 reads 'For any cap body K in R^3, I(K) <= 6'. The Introduction calls the covering conjecture the Hadwiger-Boltyanski illumination conjecture and says Boltyanski showed it equivalent to an illumination problem; the paper itself states no covering number.
event.revisions: v2 29 Jan 2026 ('Referee's comments incorporated'); journal Discrete Mathematics 349 (2026) 115025.
event.delivers: Illumination number of the class of 3D cap bodies is 6 (<= 8). This is the illumination formulation, for a class of bodies. The paper does not state a covering number for them.
event.remains: Covering number of 3D cap bodies as a covering statement; all convex bodies in dimension 3 and every n >= 4.

checked_by.who: Discrete Mathematics (refereed journal); the arXiv v2 notes incorporation of referee comments
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper (2026), with referee comments incorporated per arXiv v2 (referee identities not stated)

event.directly_checkable: The SageMath/integer LP script is cited in the paper (appendix of v1); not rerun by me.
event.direction: Consistent with the illumination form of the conjecture for 3D cap bodies (6 <= 8). Whether this is a statement about the covering number depends on the illumination-covering equivalence the paper cites, which the judging pass must weigh.

judgement.why: The statement asks for H_n <= 2^n for all n (with the parallelotope equality case); nothing settles it for any n >= 3. Gorodzha's Theorem 2 moves the covering number itself to 2^(d+O(log d)) for large d, a bound on the named quantity (its Theorem 1 is the fractional analogue and alone would be a variant); by the author's account the main argument, including the greedy covering argument for the asymptotic bound, came from GPT-6 Pro with the author checking, so generated. Arman-Bondarenko-Prymak 2024 is a journal-published bound for n = 5..8. The cap-body papers settle a class: the 3D one is stated in illumination form but the illumination/covering equivalence (Boltyanski) is classical, so I counted it as a case, digested via Discrete Mathematics; the all-dimension cap-body claim is a case, unreviewed. Graph-theoretic, spherical-valuation and covering-density items are different problems sharing the name (variant), though their own AI roles are recorded from their quotes. Pre-snapshot: Levi settles n = 2 (case); the rest are bounds or class results, so nothing pre-snapshot is whole.
judgement.doubts: Gorodzha is a three-week-old single-author v1 with no engagement; no specific error identified, so credible but unreviewed. The ChatGPT transcript was unread, so the split between model and author is from the footnote/appendix only. Translative versus homothetic forms of H_n are treated as the same quantity, as the literature does; not verified in the record. Lian-Zhang scored none because its result is unknown; Chen-Gao-Wu scored bound since its value is unread. The cap-body all-dimension claim's illumination-to-covering step relies on the standard equivalence, not a written argument.
